title.summary: CityNews describes an anti-lockdown/anti-mask rally at Chinook Centre.

scope.summary: The rally was inside the mall. CPS says its Diversity Resources Team negotiated a peaceful departure; participants dispersed and the situation was resolved.

demands.summary: Described as anti-lockdown; exact demands and governmental target are not provided.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Threshold cannot be assessed without an attendance report.

state_response.summary: Calgary Police Service negotiated participants’ peaceful departure and reported that the crowd dispersed. Later enforcement was to be considered, but no arrest or ticket is reported.

organizer.summary: A speaker/leader is mentioned but no formal organizer is identified.

notes: S021 and contemporary S028 establish an anti-mask/anti-lockdown rally at Chinook Centre, but give no participant count; threshold remains unresolved. title: Magog demonstration against COVID-19 health measures
location: Galeries Orford parking lot to Parc des Braves via Sherbrooke Street, Magog, Quebec
scope: One demonstration procession by foot and vehicle from Galeries Orford to Parc des Braves; reported arrival shortly after noon, exact start and dispersal boundary unknown
threshold_50_evidence: Local report estimates about 80, above 50; the exact number is not stated.

title.summary: Local report describes a demonstration against sanitary/health measures.

start_date.summary: Article dated Feb. 22 says “last Sunday,” identifying Feb. 21, 2021.

location.summary: Participants met at the Galeries Orford parking lot and travelled via Rue Sherbrooke to Parc des Braves in Magog.

scope.summary: One walking/vehicle procession; article says arrival at Parc des Braves shortly after noon. Exact starting time and subsequent dispersal are not stated.

demands.summary: Demonstration opposed health measures; exact policy demands are not itemized.

participants_original.summary: Local report gives an approximate count of about 80.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The reported approximate attendance is clearly over 50.

end_date.summary: Same-day procession, ending at its reported destination shortly after noon; no later end time stated.

state_response.summary: Police were present, distributed rule reminder flyers and reported five mask tickets plus one traffic ticket for phone use. Tickets are not formal arrests; all coded response fields remain unknown.

notes: Local contemporary French-language report gives an approximate count above 50 and an identifiable Quebec public-health-policy target. Five mask infraction tickets and a separate cellphone-driving ticket are recorded as reported police actions but are not coded as arrests. The route locations are one coordinated demonstration, not separate events.

title: GraceLife Church service held despite Alberta closure order
scope: Regular Sunday worship service under an AHS closure order; AHS counted attendees at 10:45 a.m.; pastor’s sermon criticized provincial COVID-19 restrictions; exact service end unknown
organizer: GraceLife Church; Pastor James Coates led the service
participants_original: AHS counted about 332 people in the sanctuary and about 57 in the lobby listening to the service.
threshold_50_evidence: AHS separately counted about 332 in the sanctuary and about 57 in the lobby during the service; both counts exceed 50, but this does not establish that attendees were protest participants.

title.summary: CityNews and AHS describe a GraceLife Sunday service held in violation of the closure order.

start_date.summary: AHS inspection report dates the service to Feb. 14, 2021.

location.summary: AHS report names GraceLife Church, 51529A Range Road 262, Parkland County; specific street details are retained in the source only.

scope.summary: AHS inspection describes a regular Sunday worship service; applicant filing says Pastor Coates preached. The service began by 10:45; exact end unknown.

organizer.summary: GraceLife Church service led by Pastor James Coates; legal filing says this is the congregation’s regular weekly worship.

demands.summary: The applicant filing says the Feb. 14 sermon criticized the Alberta Government’s COVID-19 response and health restrictions but gives no specific call for a policy change; code only the issue category while keeping protest eligibility pending.

participants_original.summary: AHS separately counted about 332 in the sanctuary and 57 in the lobby listening.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Each reported area count is above 50, although the source describes worship participants rather than protesters.

end_date.summary: The service occurred on Feb. 14; the exact physical end time is not reported.

state_response.summary: AHS and RCMP were present on Feb. 14. The filing says RCMP later asked Coates to submit to arrest; he went to the station Feb. 16 and was charged with alleged capacity, distancing and undertaking breaches. No congregation-wide arrest or dispersal is reported.

notes: Regular religious worship, not a documented rally. AHS counted 332 in the sanctuary and 57 listening from the lobby; applicant filing says the sermon criticized Alberta health restrictions and the church continued noncompliance. The codebook requires a demand-making protest, so retain pending evidence rather than infer one from worship attendance. The later court remedies were filed in May and are not event demands; the pastor’s Feb. 16 arrest is reported as a state response to continued noncompliance, not an arrest of the congregation.
open_questions: Do the Feb. 14 sermon criticism and deliberate service under closure order satisfy the demand-making protest criterion, or was this regular worship with no documented protest demand?
Exact policy ask expressed at the Feb. 14 service.
Exact service end and whether RCMP follow-up should be attributed to this specific service or cumulative noncompliance.
